items.title: Localizing away from a finite set of primes gives a semi-local ring whose maximal ideals are the maximal elements of the set
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the localization of a ring at the multiplicative set complementary to a finite union of primes: it shows that set is multiplicative and that the resulting ring is semi-local with maximal ideals in bijection with the maximal elements of the given finite set of primes. The proof checks multiplicativity directly, uses the description of the spectrum of a localization together with the avoidance lemma to see that the primes of S^{-1}A correspond to the primes of A contained in one of the p_i, and reads off the maximal ideals as the maximal elements of the finite set (proof lines 7720-7731). H2: the two-step description of the prime spectrum after localization is the substance.
